summary: This bill creates a Transportation Security Trust Fund that receives all passenger security fees, makes the money available without further appropriation solely for TSA salaries, screening, and security technology, and authorizes continued TSA operations at prior-year rates during any lapse in appropriations.

scores.thoughts: The bill establishes a dedicated Transportation Security Trust Fund using existing passenger security fees and restricts their use exclusively to aviation security purposes. It does not increase or decrease overall government spending levels, nor does it authorize new appropriations. The focus is on earmarking and continuity rather than expansion or reduction of spending.
The bill makes no changes to tax rates, fee amounts, or tax policy. It only redirects how already-collected passenger security fees are deposited and spent.
